In recent years, various threats and vulnerabilities in vehicular environments have drawn the attention of researchers and enthusiasts in both academia and industry [10, 11, 12, 13, 17, 18, 19]. Specifically, autonomous vehicles (AVs) face several security and privacy challenges. EVs extensively use the Internet Technology and Vehicle Network (V2V) communication for safety-related functions [17, 20, 21, 22, 23]. However, this open and dynamic communication network poses significant security concerns. In smart vehicles, a multitude of EV controllers using both open and closed-circuit radio with potential vulnerabilities exist. When an online communication link between two entities is formed without a mutual authentication [24, 25], an intermediate party or trusted third party is likely affected and be deceived by deception in the system. Additionally, the devices themselves are vulnerable because they are manually connected to a network and susceptible to unauthorized access. As EV communication is often with other electronic vehicles (EVs, EVs) or roadside unit (RSU), it is crucial to conduct security analysis with each of these different/low-risk internal technology A2C nodes. This raises new concerns, as information gathering can be the difference factor for safety (as seen in [26]) in the design of intelligent systems. These vulnerabilities are widely exploited owing to their low-to-no-cost architectures and ease of retail attack. As the nature of interactive AVs is dynamic, EVs also need to be provided with defense against cyber-related attacks.

This current paper identifies these vulnerabilities of intra-vehicle communication and education for the smart gateways. EV safety is improving through outstanding computational technology and control engineering, despite the problems of speedy and advanced connectivity [24, 25]. As a result, since the number of communication channels at the EV is high, it is challenging to build secure intelligence related to vehicle safety or safety function. Based on this, we identify EV communication vulnerabilities and reconstruct ISAES, an intelligent defensive system for intelligent gateways that is being deployed. The described ISAES has components that are injected with unique codes, and they use randomization algorithms regarding EV targets to provide stealth to (operationalizing and developing) the devices. Thus, the security is enhanced because our instrument is fully secured and enable efficient attacks. We demonstrate the prototype of ISAES on the Smart Gateway ASSIST platform. From this, ISAES easily leads the communication and achieves optimal performance through a full-scale analysis, over addressing ciphertexts, integrating the received messages of the EV receiver units, and the full-scan of the correctness of the computational payload. Moreover, a prototype of ISAES is also self-provisioned and presented.

In summary, we highlight, reply, and prove the security and privacy for vehicle communication. We address a very possible but nevertheless rapidly growing and productive space and call for a new potential solution for the private information transmitted inside the EV wireless environment. Additionally, we introduce and analyze the following characteristic of the hybrid vehicle-digital environment: EV mobility awareness, security, and analytic process for connectivity. This manuscript mainly focuses on ISAs and the upcoming switch but does not cover the various UAV, verge, satellite, and related aspects. Previously, a related paper only considered information integrity and confidentiality of car parking information but did not present ISAES functionality [28, 29, 30, 31]. Our contribution can be summarized as follows:

IV. Development Prospect and Upcoming Trends.

Intelligence and informatization are the most important driving forces for the development and application of smart grid. Additionally, human-computer interactions have become the key in the future and new forms of interactions. In a field of ‘smart’ ability, the human-computer should develop into 1) capability of interpretation; 2) capability of Bayesian reasoning and 3) capability of interaction. This prediction indicates a need of intertwination from smart grid growth according to the expected analysis interoperability and integration with human-computer. The smart grid will be combined with ‘Internet’, provided with intelligence and interactively controlled stimulation signals, and will provide ‘information and interaction’ from the perspective of human-computer interaction to further support future new technological applications.

The following sections will further illustrate the recent development trends and its specific use cases.

I. Development of Vehicular Information system

(Figure omitted) is a comprehensive multimodal sensing system constructed for transforming the multimodal unstructured information from the automobile into a multidisciplinary and practical decision information. This system carefully addresses the spectrum of vehicular data, which include: 1) interior and exterior, both of which contain diverse information and traditional logic intelligence data and sensor data; 2) physical, perceptive and artificial intelligence data, which include: road condition, vehicle status and driving environment, etc.

The system 1) assigns and manages the road from its edge to the end, identifies road conditions, initiate warning messages and analyze accident, and its structure constitutes a benchmark for the integration of vehicular intelligent transportation systems. The smart data acquired from the road includes road image, front and rear position, speed, traffic, condition and environmental information; 2) facilitates a comprehensive hierarchical generalization of the data through a process called multi-dimensional clustering, and based on these features intelligent and completed the safety, comfort and mobility through the automated driving service system. The built V-I-D (Visual-Information-Dynamic) system (Syngrows, 2021) is responsible for accepting the video and radar sensor data, which can help to gather road information and extract all information through the categorization of image detection processing, car state detection (whether the car is in motion or stopped), registration of rules, analysis of results and detection of warning messages.

Nassif and Issa (2017) have developed one new multisensory collection unit for recognizing gradually changing traffic rules with its extreme environment, which involves six kinds of information, such as: dynamic RGB images, ranging, event scanning, depth and height mapping and mainline video surveillance. At the lower equipment, there is a low-frequency event sensor with a bandwidth capable of a range of 3,500 Hz. At the higher equipment, there is a high-frequency event sensor with a bandwidth of 1,000 Hz for frontal cameras and high-resolution 8-bit color single lens system camera. Therefore, this aim for traffic surveillance can be utilized for setting supremates for intelligent environment such as image recognition, traffic analysis and detecting warning messages at any time according to the needs of vehicular traffic rate, and then establish an all-round evaluation and optimization system that will drive the system to a high value in terms of subjective and objective.

The smart system’s design incorporates the technology of artificial intelligence integration and innovation. Trained by artificial intelligence, these systems in vehicular visual navigation and environment intelligence have the ability to make a large-scale integration of distributed traffic scenes, a large number of rules, automatic procession, and highly flexible operation. The current situation of these systems shows the advantages of operation and operation in dynamic change.

For SEVs, functional safety becomes of highest relevance since we are dealing with more complexity in the electrical powertrain and autonomous driving functionalities. The automotive industry has consequently established rigorous procedures for designing fail-safe systems, and in the operational context these systems commonly are subjected to extensive testing to ensure that they remain safe even if they fail. For SEVs, the battery management system (BMS) is also an essential component for functional safety as it observes the state of charge, temperature, and health of the battery. One potential risk is a malfunction of the battery management system, which may cause overcharging, overheating, and in the worst case, possible runaway.

### 3. Security and Safety Integration

The automotive domain is digitalizing and becoming connected, which makes it next to mandatory to integrate cyber security and functional safety. Although the two domains evolved separately, they must merge in SEVs, as the failure of one system can put the other at risk.

4. Simulation and Experimental Setup

Simulations were carried out in MATLAB/Simulink for a five-phase inverter system with SiC-based power modules. Fault scenarios, including short-circuits, phase loss, and thermal overload, were simulated, and fault detection time, isolation rate, and thermal characteristics were studied. Experimental validation was done with a lab-scale 5-level SiC-based inverter system, where hardware fault injection was employed to inject faults and to evaluate system responses under real physical conditions. Performance indicators, namely, the fault detection time, the fault isolation time and temperature rise were observed.

5. Evaluation Criteria

The performance of the system was evaluated against:

• Detection Time: Time from the fault occurrence until the time detected.

• Phase Isolation time: Is the time taken to isolate the faulty phase.

• Discharge and Thermal Stress: Time to discharge energy in a safe manner and impact on thermal response.

• System Availability: Ability to keep running with the rest of the healthy phases after fault localization and clearance.

The fault-protection schemes developed in this paper provide full-scope safety and reliability features to the multi-phase inverters in SEVs. The pragmatic combination of cyber security and functional safety supports fast fault detection, phase disconnection and safe energy discharge, thus minimizing thermal strain and preventing system failure.

Result

The simulation results show that the proposed fault protection strategies can significantly improve the reliability and safety of multi-phase inverter in SEVs. The high speed centralized short-circuit detection system isolates faults quickly and the active short-circuiting and hybrid discharging technology eliminates thermal overloads, providing no-break continuity of service. Practical Validation confirms that the processes in the system are capable of handling the fault conditions both effectively (by minimizing the possibilities to damage valuable components) and efficiently.

D-Safety and security The confidentiality, integrity availability of data between vehicle systems and real-time communication to external entities are fundamentally important. The incorporation of security considerations as described here must be employed in safety-related systems to protect those systems from unauthorized access. As emphasized by Fang et al. 2021), the hazards and risks of such cyber security break may immediately affect functional safety, which substantiates the necessity of a comprehensive framework encompassing both areas. Standing in the way is the ever-changing landscape of computer security threats, and safety-critical system design. As SEVs begin to integrate greater levels of autonomy and connectivity, the complexity of their safety and security systems will grow and there will be a need for more flexible solutions to mitigate new threats as they appear. Robustness and adaptiveness functions, which enable detecting and responding to new kind of threats, are paramount in ensuring operational soundness of SEVs. This is in accordance with Marupaka et al. 2021), emphasizing the significance of continuous control and adaptation of security procedures to dynamic cyber risks. Cybersecurity and functional safety must be combined not only in SEVs but is an issue for the automotive sector as a whole. Development of consistent standards and models that can address both areas with coherence will be of paramount importance to guarantee the safety, security and reliability of the future vehicles. With the transformation of the industry from semi-autonomous to autonomous vehicles, the role of cyber security in protecting the vehicle control systems from external attack will be even more essential. 3 Summary It can be concluded that successful cyber-security and functional-safety integration will be a fundamental enabler for the realization of safe and secure SEV systems. This work then establishes a holistic control framework for handling the two domains, so that these vehicles can be operated safely and securely, in spite of complicated failures or cyber-attacks. Future work could focus on refinement of these integrated approaches with an emphasis on realtime monitoring, machine learning for threat detection, and the development of agile standards that can accommodate the fast-changing reality of connected and autonomous vehicles.
